title: Bengal to spend Rs 1,000 crore on old temples under 'Tirtha Kshetra Circuit', Adhikari says
dek: The Chief Minister restated a two-year temple renovation plan first announced in July, and said Gangasagar Mela has been declared an international fair.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Friday that the West Bengal government will spend Rs 1,000 crore over the next two years renovating old Hindu temples and monasteries across the state, under a programme he has named the "Tirtha Kshetra Circuit", or pilgrimage circuit.

"We will spend Rs 1,000 crore in the next two years to renovate all the old Hindu monasteries and temples," Mr Adhikari said while inaugurating a community Kali Puja at Aranghata in Nadia district, according to reports. He said the work would cover ancient temples run by religious institutions, trusts and the public, not only private sites, and cited the redevelopment of Kedarnath, Badrinath, Ayodhya, Varanasi and Ujjain's Mahakal temple under Prime Minister Narendra Modi as the model.

## What was announced

The scheme was first announced in July, when Mr Adhikari described a Rs 1,000 crore, two-year programme for ancient temples and maths at a meeting at Nabanna before the Rath Yatra, reports at the time said. Friday's speech restated the amount and timeline and gave the programme its formal name.

One Bengali report said the circuit would run from the Madanmohan temple in Cooch Behar through Kalighat, Tarakeswar and Dakshineswar. The government has not yet published guidelines on which temples will qualify, how they will be selected or which department will carry out the work. In July, the state named Jalpesh temple in Jalpaiguri, a temple in the Jayanti area near the Bhutan border and Tarakeswar as the first pilgrimage centres to get support, and said Rs 15 crore of work was under way at the Tarakeswar temple complex.

## Other announcements

In the same speech, the Chief Minister said:

- Chandannagar in Hooghly and Krishnanagar in Nadia will be decorated by the state for Jagaddhatri Puja, and he will attend in both towns.
- Nabadwip and Shantipur in Nadia, and Cooch Behar, will be decorated for Ras Purnima; he plans to attend in Nabadwip.
- The Gangasagar Mela, held each January at the mouth of the Hooghly, has been declared an "international fair".

He also contrasted this year's festival season with that under the previous Trinamool Congress government. "Earlier, Durga idol immersions often faced problems. This year, there was no restriction or hurdle anywhere," he said, according to reports.

## Background

Spending public money on places of worship has been a point of contention in Bengal politics. The previous government, led by Mamata Banerjee, built a Jagannath temple at Digha, which opened in April 2025, and gave annual grants to Durga Puja committees. In December 2024, as Leader of the Opposition, Mr Adhikari said funds from the state exchequer could not be used to build the Digha temple, according to reports at the time. On Friday he described the new programme as the restoration of existing old temples and monasteries.

No response from the Trinamool Congress, the CPI(M) or the Congress to Friday's announcement had been reported by Friday evening.

## What happens next

The state is expected to set out how the money will be spent and which temples will be included. The Chief Minister is due at Jagaddhatri Puja in Chandannagar and Krishnanagar and at Ras Purnima in Nabadwip in the coming weeks.
